  "screen_decision": "exclude",
  "screen_rationale": "The study compares human genome-wide association studies (GWAS) with pharmaceutical research and development, but it does not report any quantitative measure of agreement between non-human animal results and human clinical results. The study focuses on the overlap between genetic studies and drug development efforts, not on the concordance of animal models with human outcomes.",
  "arm": "disease-biology",
  "arm_evidence": "The study focuses on disease coverage and the overlap of GWAS and pharmaceutical research and development, aiming to understand how genetic analyses and drug development efforts align.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "cross-cutting"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The study analyzes a broad range of human diseases and drug development efforts across multiple therapeutic areas, rather than focusing on a single one.",
  "model_type": "regulatory-dataset",
  "model_evidence": "The study analyzes data from pharmaceutical research and development, including drug indications and clinical development stages, which aligns with the scope of regulatory datasets.",
  "species": [
    "not-species-specific"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The study focuses on human diseases and human genetic studies (GWAS), and does not analyze or report on any specific non-human animal species.",
  "endpoint_class": "secondary-biomarker",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study discusses disease coverage, overlap between GWAS and drug development, and target-disease indication pairings, which are more akin to biomarkers or intermediate outcomes rather than hard clinical endpoints like mortality or survival."
